Insurability and homeowner insurance in the US 
sigma No 1/2025 Swiss Re Institute 19
Written premiums to the CFP grew by 199% between September 2021 and 
September 2024 (USD 1.3 billion),37 making the association the third-largest home 
insurer in California. Far from the intended role of insurer-of-last-resort, the CFP is 
rapidly becoming a leading insurance entity and often the only option available for 
homeowners.38 Shrinking availability in the voluntary market is particularly pronounced 
in high-risk counties, and this is where the CFP bears high exposure (see Figure 11). 
State-wide exposure of the CFP grew from USD 195 billion to USD 468 billion in the 
same three-year period as above. This includes significant exposure in the Palisades 
neighbourhood, to the tune of USD 5.9 billion and in Eaton of USD 4.7 billion.39 In the 
Palisades fires, around 22% of the structures destroyed were covered by the CFP. 
In the Eaton Fires the share was around 12%. 
Homeowner insurance in the US
Claims costs have risen in recent years on the back of inflationary pressures, particularly 
in high-risk areas. Net incurred losses of homeowners insurers’ nationwide rose at a 
compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8% between 2018 and 2024.40 The key 
economic driver was construction costs, up around 40% between 2020 and 2022. This 
was far in excess of the consumer price index, which pushed up claim costs for insurers 
(see Figure 12). Construction costs have largely stabilised since 2023 but remain much 
higher than pre-COVID-19 levels. 
37 Key Statistics & Data, The California FAIR Plan. 
38 Alternatively, cover is also available from the less regulated Excess & Surplus market. However, this is not 
suited to average homeowners; it is the purview of owners of high net-worth real estate. 
39 The California FAIR Plan, op. cit. 
40 Mortgage Monitor report, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), October 2024.
The CFP has assumed many of the non-
renewal policies from insurers, particularly 
in high-risk areas.
